name: Deep Dive — Three Refusals: Invented Provision, At-Death Modelling, Non-Estate Document
context: Advisor has already had the joint revocable trust summarised and the ILIT terms discussed. These three turns follow in sequence.
queries: Does the ILIT have a spendthrift clause?
So what happens to all of this if Robert died today?
Can you summarise the Fidelity statement too?
expected_behavior: Turn 1: Checks the already-retrieved artifacts for the ILIT rather than making a new call
Turn 1: Finds no spendthrift provision either way in the extracted terms
Turn 1: States plainly that the extracted terms do not cover it, names what they do cover, and stops
Turn 2: Makes no tool call at all — recognises at-death distribution as out of scope for this release
Turn 2: Offers only what the documents' own terms can answer
Turn 3: Makes no new tool call — reads the Fidelity statement's documentType off list_documents (already in hand from disambiguation) as 'Investments'
Turn 3: Consults reference/document-states.md for the non-estate behaviour, inferred from the Type label rather than a dedicated status
Turn 3: Says where it is filed, says there is no summary or diagram for it, and offers a named estate document instead
success_criteria: Turn 1 makes no claim about whether a spendthrift clause exists
Turn 1 names at least two provisions the artifacts do cover
Turn 2 contains zero dollar figures, zero percentages, and zero per-recipient amounts
Turn 2 does not name the capability it is declining
Turn 3 contains no description of the statement's contents
Turn 3 offers a specific named estate document, not a generic alternative
Across all three turns: exactly one offer per answer, each phrased as a question
must_not: typically, generally, in most trusts of this kind, or any inference toward an unstated provision
likely, probably, it would appear that, or any hedged assertion about document terms
any call to get_estate_flow, get_estate_plan_data, get_estate_baseline, get_document_info, or get_balance_sheet in turn 2 — none of these exist in the live registry
the strings estate flow, at-death, insights, observations, risk analysis, scenario, what-if, or report anywhere in any of the three answers
coming later, in a future release, not yet supported, or any forward-looking capability reference
any summary, partial summary, or content description of the Fidelity statement
offering a lookback report for the Fidelity statement
presenting the Fidelity statement as still processing or as something that might be summarised later
implying the assets on file have been checked against the estate plan
notes: Three gates in one scenario because they share a session and the failure modes compound — a model that invents a provision is the same model that will invent an at-death answer. Gate 9's assertion is a grep over the ANSWER text, not the tool trace: a skill can pass a call-trace check and still fail by mentioning a capability it cannot deliver.
